feature1.prompt: Feature 1: Enhance the ReadOnlyPasswordHashField by setting its disabled property to True by default. Currently, the field does not enforce a read-only behavior which might lead to accidental or unintended modifications. After this fix, the field will automatically render as non-editable by using the disabled HTML attribute. This change ensures that any user-submitted value is ignored in favor of the field's initial data, improving security and reducing the risk of password mishandling.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature focuses on updating the ReadOnlyPasswordHashField implementation. Developers should modify the __init__ method in django/contrib/auth/forms.py to include 'kwargs.setdefault("disabled", True)'. The aim is to ensure that the field becomes non-editable by default. Care must be taken to preserve existing behavior related to initial data handling and to make sure the field ignores any altered input.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/contrib/auth/forms.py, within the ReadOnlyPasswordHashField class, specifically in the __init__ method where the disabled property should be set.

feature2.prompt: Feature 2: Refactor the UserChangeForm by removing the clean_password method. Currently, the clean_password method returns the initial password value to avoid unwanted changes, but this becomes redundant thanks to the improved disabled behavior of the password field. Removing this method simplifies the form logic and eliminates the potential pitfall of relying on a custom implementation. The form should automatically retain the original password value without requiring an explicit clean_password method.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature involves removing the clean_password method from the UserChangeForm in django/contrib/auth/forms.py. Developers should locate and delete the clean_password method from the UserChangeForm class. It is essential to verify that any forms extending UserChangeForm continue to function correctly and that no dependencies on this method exist. The removal should simplify the form's password handling logic while maintaining overall security.
feature2.entrypoint: File: django/contrib/auth/forms.py, within the UserChangeForm class, specifically remove the clean_password method (as shown in the patch around lines 163-169).

collaboration_points.shared_resources: The django/contrib/auth/forms.py file, specifically the ReadOnlyPasswordHashField and UserChangeForm classes, along with any custom forms that extend these components.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature 1 introduces a secure, non-editable password hash field by setting the disabled property, which Feature 2 relies on by removing the redundant clean_password method. Both features affect the same module and must operate cohesively, so the integration should verify that the simplified UserChangeForm properly works with the updated ReadOnlyPasswordHashField.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on each feature should discuss the modifications to form initialization and password handling. Coordination is required to ensure that any custom forms or dependencies are updated accordingly and that the integrated changes do not introduce regressions in password processing.
